Commercial flights generally avoid flying directly over the Himalayas due to severe safety risks, including extreme high-altitude terrain, limited emergency landing options, severe turbulence, and risks associated with cabin depressurization. While not a strict no-fly zone, the "roof of the world" poses dangers to navigation and passenger safety, making alternative routes safer and more efficient.
